questions.text: Day trading involves holding positions overnight to capture longer-term trends.
questions.explanation: Day trading requires closing all positions before the session ends, leaving no overnight exposure.

questions.text: Which describes the risk control principle of setting position size based on a fixed percent risk per trade?
options: Adjust position size so that potential profit equals 2% of account.
Set stop-loss distance so that loss if hit equals a small fixed percent of account equity.
Use a fixed number of shares regardless of volatility.
Increase position size after each winning trade to compound gains.
questions.explanation: Position size is set so that the stop-loss loss equals the predetermined risk percent per trade.

questions.text: Which time period offers the highest liquidity and volatility for a trader in Atlantic Standard Time?
questions.explanation: The London‑New York overlap from 9:30‑11:30 AM AST is cited as the most liquid/volatile window.

questions.text: What is the effect of trading during off‑peak hours on transaction cost?
options: Bid‑ask spread widens, increasing cost for the same trade size.
Transaction cost remains constant regardless of liquidity.
Off‑peak trading eliminates the bid‑ask spread.
questions.explanation: The bid‑ask spread is wide off‑peak, making off‑peak trading more expensive for the same trades.
